messages:
maria: Kicking off a small experiment: 'token-tilt' admit calibration for the continuous batcher. Goal: reduce end-user p95 regressions when KV-miss batches trigger slow kernels, while keeping throughput. TL;DR: per-lane token-budget + tilt weight to favor low-token requests during bursts.

aj: Curious — how does this differ from the existing per-request fair lanes?

maria: Instead of equal token cap across lanes, we compute a dynamic tilt factor based on recent kernel latency mismatch and KV hit-rate. Tilt reduces max tokens for lanes that caused kernel slowdowns in the last 30s.

sam: Can you paste the config snippet?

maria: Sure — prototype:

```json
{
  "batcher": "continuous",
  "admit": {
    "mode": "token_tilt",
    "base_token_cap": 1024,
    "tilt_window_s": 30,
    "tilt_decay": 0.6,
    "kv_miss_penalty": 0.8
  },
  "queue": {
    "lane_count": 4,
    "per_lane_budget_enabled": true
  }
}
```

devon: Nice. What are the expected failure modes? e.g., will small chat messages get favored too much and starve long completions?

maria: Good call. We add a soft floor to ensure long requests still make progress: min_tokens_per_req=64. Also a slowpath that can request emergency allocation if request waits >1500ms.

aj: How are we protecting against oscillation (tilt flipping lanes back and forth)?

maria: Tilt is smoothed with exponential decay (tilt_decay) + hop suppression: once a lane's tilt changed >10% we lock adjustments for 10s.

sam: Any profiling data yet?

perf-bot: recent-run: kernel-mismatch spike at t=2026-03-12T14:02Z, kv-miss-rate 18%, p95-latency +22% on gpt-xx-emu kernel. Baseline batcher queueing shows large batches with >6 long contexts coalesced -> kernel swap overhead ~120ms.

maria: Right — the idea is to avoid forming those big mixed batches when they include several KV-miss long-context requests. Tilt will bias grouping so smaller token requests coalesce together and large ones are admitted more conservatively.

devon: How are we measuring success? Metrics?

maria: Primary: p95 latency for interactive lanes (-target 10%); secondary: tokens/sec throughput loss <= 5%; third: 429 count should not increase more than +2% relative to baseline. Also track kernel-flip frequency.

aj: 429s — we should be explicit: prefer soft-shed (deferred admission + retry advice) vs hard 429s. Do we change response shape?

maria: We'll emit soft-shed header X-Redwood-Shed: soft and a Retry-After hint when we delay. Hard 429 only when queue depth exceeds emergency threshold.

sam: Any safety toggles for rollout?

maria: Canary on 5% of hosts, ramp to 25% if p95 improves; auto-roll back if p95 regresses or 429s spike. Also allow per-customer opt-out.

infra-bot: deploy-batch-plan: canary=2026-03-14T09:00Z -> 5% -> monitor 2h -> if OK 25% -> monitor 4h -> full. (alerts: p95>baseline+5% OR 429s>baseline+3%)

devon: One more thought — KV prefetch behaviour interacts strongly. If tilt penalizes KV-miss lanes, it could reduce prefetch opportunities and raise later miss-rate. Need to couple with prefetch heuristics.

maria: Agreed. We'll add a coupling signal: if prefetch success drops >5% we reduce tilt_penalty by half for 60s.

aj: I can run a short cluster sim today to test oscillation scenarios.

maria: Thanks! I'll push the prototype config to the experiment branch and add dashboard cards: p95_by_lane, token_throughput, kernel_flip_rate, kv_miss_by_lane.

sam: Ping when dashboards are up. Also include examples of the soft-shed header in the docs so SDKs can surface UX.

maria: Will do. Next: data review in #eng-runtime-sync Tue 10am. :rocket:

perf-bot: note: saved profiling snapshot id=pf-20260312-4477 for postmortem if needed.

aj: Looking forward to the sim results. Good job outlining risk controls.

maria: thanks — updates coming as we get numbers. :thumbsup:
